business_patterns.top_pattern: Authorization and facility mapping shifts need validation first
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: Authorization coding and facility classification for inpatient claims
key_driver_codes: Septicemia or Severe Sepsis without Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours without MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: A meaningful share of the increase sits in authorization code movement and claims classified to Not Mapped facility buckets rather than a clean care-delivery trend. The largest signals are in GA and CA authorization coding, with additional unmapped facility growth in GA, PA, KY, OH, and CA. Business action should wait until the authorization-to-claim and facility mapping logic is confirmed.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: If these shifts are coding or mapping artifacts, UM, reimbursement, and network actions would target the wrong root cause.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Run a focused audit of authorization code assignment and facility mapping for the cited states, reconcile whether claims moved into AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION or Not Mapped buckets, and only then route confirmed findings to UM or contracting.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Authorization code distribution and unmapped facility classification may reflect coding or mapping movement rather than true utilization or reimbursement change.
evidence_summary: GA AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION added about +$1.7M, led by Aftercare with CC/MCC at +$1.0M and Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC at +$623K.
CA AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION added about +$1.1M, led by electrolyte disorders with MCC at +$696K and sepsis without prolonged ventilation at +$409K.
Facility classified as Not Mapped added about +$417K in GA, +$143K in PA, +$126K in KY, with smaller additional impacts in OH and CA.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Secondary markets show concentrated authorized inpatient growth
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: PPO Local authorized inpatient use across KY, CT, GA, NY, VA, OH, NV, and ME
business_patterns.pattern_details: Outside the largest markets, authorized inpatient growth is recurring across acute hospital, rehab, and critical access settings. Most of the increase is volume-led, but several markets also show higher paid per admit, especially in KY and smaller mixed-pressure pockets. The pattern is concentrated enough at named providers and facility types to support targeted UM and local network action rather than a broad national response.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Recurring growth across multiple smaller markets can accumulate into a material trend and often reflects local admission management or provider concentration issues.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Prioritize market-by-market reviews for KY, VA, OH, CT, NY, NV, and ME to confirm admission drivers, then target local UM controls and provider discussions where growth is concentrated at specific facilities or providers.
evidence_summary: KY acute hospital PPO Local added about +$497K on 16 more admissions, with roughly +$1.6K paid per admit.
VA growth at MARY WASHINGTON HOSPITAL INC added about +$345K on 25 more admissions.
OH added about +$300K in acute hospital use and another +$264K in Physical Rehab.
CT, GA, and NY acute hospital utilization added about +$443K, with MANCHESTER MEMORIAL HOSPITAL at +$81K and HIGHLAND HOSPITAL at +$72K among notable contributors.

business_patterns.top_pattern: CA authorized inpatient and rehab use is climbing
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA / PPO Local / ACUTE HOSPITAL and Physical Rehab / authorized inpatient
key_driver_codes: Miscellaneous Disorders of Nutrition, Metabolism, and Fluids and Electrolytes with MCC
Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: In CA, authorized PPO Local inpatient spend is rising across both acute hospital and post-acute rehab settings. Acute hospital growth is mainly admission-driven across electrolyte disorders, UTI, and sepsis, while Physical Rehab adds a separate aftercare cost lift with higher paid per admit. This points to a combined inpatient and downstream site-of-care management opportunity.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: When acute admissions and follow-on rehab both rise, total episode cost can accelerate even without a broad reimbursement change.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Review CA admission appropriateness and discharge pathways together, with special focus on aftercare cases flowing into Physical Rehab and on sepsis, UTI, and electrolyte admissions in acute hospital.
evidence_summary: CA acute hospital utilization added about +$413K, led by electrolyte disorders with MCC at +$159K, UTI without MCC at +$136K, and sepsis without prolonged ventilation at +$118K.
CA Physical Rehab added about +$593K in Aftercare with CC/MCC on 9 more admissions.
Physical Rehab also showed about +$2.4K higher paid per admit, indicating cost pressure beyond volume alone.

business_patterns.top_pattern: CA medical aftercare, sepsis, and electrolyte cases are concentrating
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA clinical case mix in unclassified inpatient medical cases
business_patterns.pattern_details: CA also has a concentrated medical case-mix story behind the operational growth. The largest contributors are aftercare following neoplasm surgery, sepsis, and electrolyte or fluid disorders, with both higher admissions and some higher severity signals. This is a focused clinical concentration, not a broad spread across many unrelated diagnoses.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A concentrated clinical mix can support more precise UM and clinical pathway intervention than a broad utilization response.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Send the CA cluster for clinical and UM review focused on aftercare management, sepsis pathways, and electrolyte/fluid admissions to determine which cases are preventable, redirectable, or appropriate for alternative post-acute management.
evidence_summary: Aftercare following neoplasm surgery in Aftercare with CC/MCC added about +$369K.
Sepsis unspecified organism added about +$263K on 26 more admissions.
Hyponatremia, hypernatremia, and fluid overload together added about +$344K.
Other gram-negative sepsis added about +$112K on 14 more admissions.

business_patterns.top_pattern: CA has a cluster of rare catastrophic aftercare cases
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA rare high-cost aftercare and catastrophic inpatient cases
key_driver_codes: UNS INJURY C4 LEVEL C-SPN CORD SUB
ENC SURG AFTERCARE FOLLOW SURG NS
TRAUMATIC SA HEMORRHAGE NO LOC SUB
TRAUM SUBDURAL HEM LOC UNS DUR SUB
business_patterns.pattern_details: A separate CA pattern is being driven by a small number of very high-cost aftercare and catastrophic neurological cases. These are low-volume events, but each admission carries outsized spend and they are concentrated in aftercare-related inpatient billing. This requires individual case review rather than a broad policy change.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A handful of catastrophic cases can materially move spend and need different intervention than recurring medical utilization.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Perform case-level review of these CA admissions to confirm clinical appropriateness, benefit configuration, and post-acute planning before considering any broader utilization policy response.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The pattern is driven by very small case counts and unusually high spend per admission, so individual case validation is needed before broader action.
evidence_summary: Rare CA high-cost cases added about +$830K and were concentrated in Aftercare with CC/MCC.
A single C4 spinal cord injury aftercare case added about +$175K.
Traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage and surgical aftercare each added about +$164K to +$173K.
Additional traumatic cerebral and subdural hemorrhage cases added about +$222K combined.

business_patterns.top_pattern: GA authorized acute and rehab use is getting more expensive
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: GA / PPO Local / ACUTE HOSPITAL and Physical Rehab / authorized inpatient
key_driver_codes: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: GA shows combined volume and unit-cost pressure in authorized acute hospital and Physical Rehab settings. Acute hospital growth is concentrated in cellulitis and UTI admissions, and EMORY HOSPITAL PERRY appears as a smaller but notable provider concentration with higher paid per admit. The rehab component suggests follow-on aftercare cost pressure as well.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: GA is not only admitting more cases in key medical DRGs, it is also paying more per case in parts of the flow.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Target GA for joint UM and network review, focusing on cellulitis and UTI admission management, rehab referral patterns, and provider-level pricing or billing variance where spend is concentrated.
evidence_summary: GA acute hospital PPO Local added about +$491K, led by Cellulitis without MCC at +$213K and Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC at +$206K.
EMORY HOSPITAL PERRY added about +$72K on 8 more admissions with roughly +$3.7K paid per admit.
GA Physical Rehab added about +$122K in Aftercare with CC/MCC with roughly +$7.4K paid per admit.

business_patterns.top_pattern: GA UTI and cellulitis admissions are driving case mix
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: GA clinical case mix in unclassified inpatient medical cases
business_patterns.pattern_details: GA's clinical concentration is centered on urinary tract infection and cellulitis admissions. UTI diagnoses are largely volume-driven, while the cellulitis cases also carry some higher paid-per-admit pressure. This gives GA a focused medical-management opportunity aligned to the operational acute hospital trend.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: The same few diagnoses are repeatedly driving spend, which makes intervention more actionable than a diffuse inpatient trend.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Route GA cases for clinical and UM review on UTI and cellulitis admission pathways, including avoidable admission screening and post-discharge management for recurrence-prone patients.
evidence_summary: UTI site not specified added about +$261K on 31 more admissions.
Acute cystitis without hematuria and pyonephrosis added about +$101K and +$94K.
Cellulitis of the left and right lower limb added about +$125K and +$90K, with higher paid-per-admit pressure in those cells.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Scattered one-off complex admissions are emerging across multiple states
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: Rare low-volume complex inpatient cases across CT, GA, NY, PA, and VA
key_driver_codes: Septicemia or Severe Sepsis without Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours with MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: Several states show one-off or very low-volume complex admissions that are individually expensive but not yet recurring enough to support broad policy changes. The biggest cluster is a mix of isolated cardiac, surgical, gastrointestinal, neurologic, sepsis, endocrine, pneumonia, and neoplasm cases spread across a small set of providers. This is best handled through targeted case review and data-quality confirmation, not broad network or authorization rule changes.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: These cases can distort trend lines and should be separated from recurring utilization patterns before leadership acts on them.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Review these cases individually for clinical appropriateness, diagnosis and DRG accuracy, and provider-specific concentration, then decide whether any should migrate into a formal outlier management or data-quality workflow.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Most of the signal comes from single-admission or two-admission events with low baseline volume, so case-level validation is required before broad action.
evidence_summary: A diversified multi-state rare-case cluster added about +$435K, including a Not Mapped case at ATLANTICARE REGIONAL MEDICAL CTR at +$41K and several one-off surgical and cardiac cases at MARY WASHINGTON HOSPITAL INC.
Sepsis with MCC one-off cases across CT, GA, and VA added about +$90K.
Smaller endocrine, brain neoplasm, and pneumonia outlier cases added about +$74K combined.

executive_summary.headline: The strongest business story is a mix of validation-sensitive authorization and mapping shifts, plus recurring authorized inpatient growth concentrated in CA, GA, and several secondary markets.
executive_summary.primary_business_message: Validation comes first because nearly $3.9M of apparent change is tied to authorization code distribution and unmapped facility classification. Once that is cleared, the next priority is operational action on authorized acute hospital and rehab growth, especially in CA and GA, followed by focused clinical review of concentrated medical case mix and a separate workflow for rare catastrophic or one-off complex admissions.
recommended_focus_order: Validate authorization coding and facility mapping before taking broad action.
Address authorized inpatient and rehab growth in CA, GA, and secondary markets with UM and network levers.
Separate recurring clinical concentrations from rare outlier cases and route them to the right clinical review path.

notes: All 30 analytical groups were assigned to 8 business patterns.
Validation issues were intentionally consolidated into one gating pattern to avoid acting on coding or mapping artifacts.
Several lower-materiality segments were merged into broader secondary-market and rare-outlier patterns to stay within the 8-pattern limit while preserving distinct business actions.
